intro: If you're heading to Buriram and want a room for just over a thousand baht that still gets you a nice pool to soak in, a gym you can actually train in, and easy parking — Ray Hotel Buriram is a name guests bring up for its value. One Thai review site summed it up as "hundred-baht prices, thousand-baht service." It's a 3-star hotel on Bulamduan Road in Isan Subdistrict, within Buriram city, opened in 2014 and renovated in 2019. Rooms start at about THB 1,070/night, the overall score sits in the 8.3–8.4 range, and it has pulled in several hundred reviews across multiple platforms.

body.html: Who Ray Hotel suits — The shortest possible summary: Ray Hotel Buriram is a small hotel of around 44 rooms that plays the "value" card pretty well · It isn't a luxury property where everything is polished, and it isn't a stadium-side resort where you can cross the street to watch a match · It's a 3-star hotel within Buriram city that hands you a set of amenities well beyond what just-over-a-thousand-baht usually buys, especially the saltwater pool and a genuinely well-equipped gym · It opened back in 2014 and had a big renovation around 2019, and it's still running well today, with an overall score in the 8.3–8.4 range from several hundred reviews · Real reviews line up on who fits best here: families who drive in themselves, people visiting Buriram on a tight budget who still want a pool for the kids and a clean, quiet room, and fitness-minded travellers who want a gym at the hotel · Another group that says it left impressed are people using Buriram as a base to drive out to Phanom Rung and Prasat Muang Tam, since there's free parking and the location makes it easy to get onto the main road toward other districts · As for anyone chasing luxury, brand-new rooms in every corner, or stepping out the door into a sea of restaurants, this place may not quite hit the mark, because the hotel sits on a quieter lane away from the heart of the commercial district

Location and getting around — Ray Hotel is at 515 Moo 8, Bulamduan Road, Isan Subdistrict, within Mueang Buriram district · The distance from the city centre runs about 1.3–2.8 kilometres depending on your reference point, so it's still in town, a few minutes' drive to the market or restaurants in the city · The point many people care about is the distance to the sports venues: about 3.8 kilometres from Chang Arena and about 4.3 kilometres from Chang International Circuit · Compared with many city-centre hotels that sit 9–10 kilometres from the stadium, Ray Hotel's location is an advantage for anyone coming for football or the races, since travel time on match day is shorter · It's also only about 2.1 kilometres from Buriram railway station, handy for those arriving by train · Buriram Airport (BFV) is about 35 kilometres away, roughly a 35–40 min drive, which is normal for Buriram's airport since it's outside the city anyway · The location note that comes up most in reviews is the hotel entrance — many people agree that if you drive in following the map pin for the first time you can easily get lost, because you have to turn into a fairly narrow lane. The advice is to keep GPS running and drive slowly as you get close, or call the front desk for directions ahead of time

"The pool is great, the saltwater doesn't sting your eyes, easy to soak in, the kids played all afternoon · The gym has more machines than I expected for a hotel at this price · The only catch is the narrow entrance lane — got a little lost driving in the first time."

Room types and decor — Ray Hotel has around 44 rooms in total, split across several types · It starts with the Deluxe Room at roughly 30 sqm, available both as a twin (two single beds) and as a Queen Deluxe with a single king bed, which is wider than the standard room at many 3-star hotels in town · Stepping up, there's the Deluxe Room for 3 guests at roughly 35 sqm, suited to a small family or three friends, plus Family Room (a king bed with a single bed) and Executive Room, with some packages including gym access · A point many reviews praise is that every room is air-conditioned with a private balcony, a safe, a tea/coffee maker, a flat-screen TV, and a shower bathroom · Plenty of guests say the rooms are clean, quiet, and the beds comfortable, which earns consistent praise · But to be straight about it, some voices note that certain rooms are fairly dark and get little natural light, because the windows or the orientation of some rooms don't catch much sun · A few reviews also mention that bedside reading lamps and outlets are limited, so anyone who likes to read before bed or needs to charge several devices may feel it's not enough · This is a small detail you can fix with a power strip and by setting expectations to match a 3-star price, rather than a major problem

Amenities, the pool, and the gym — This is what puts Ray Hotel on the list for anyone after good value · The number-one highlight people mention most is the saltwater infinity pool of roughly 24x8 metres with a separate kids' pool · The upside of saltwater is that it doesn't sting the eyes or reek of chlorine like a typical pool, so many reviews praise how easy it is to soak in and how long the kids can play without irritation · The second highlight is the gym with more than 30 machines, including large treadmills and weight machines, which is bigger and more serious than the tiny gyms hotels at this price usually have · At times there's a trainer on hand, so plenty of fitness-minded travellers pick this place because they don't have to pause their training schedule while travelling · There's also a massage room, a restaurant and bar, free parking, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk, and a meeting room for seminar groups · An airport shuttle is available but it's an add-on service with an extra charge, so book it ahead · It's only fair to say the common areas aren't spacious or luxurious, since it's a small hotel, but in terms of "what you get for what you pay," the saltwater pool plus a big gym is a selling point you don't often find among the city's 3-star hotels

Food and bar — Breakfast is another part guests speak especially well of · The hotel serves a breakfast buffet with both Thai and Western dishes. Many reviews praise the wide choice and decent flavours for the price, with people saying "breakfast is tasty, lots to choose from," a compliment that comes up again and again · The buffet usually runs about 7:00 AM–10:00 AM and is often included in the room rate for many packages; if you book without it, you can add it for a reasonable price · Beyond breakfast there's an in-house restaurant and bar for dinner or a light drink · That said, because the hotel sits on a fairly quiet lane some distance from the dense restaurant areas, many people choose to drive out for dinner in the city rather than eat every meal at the hotel, which is exactly why free parking is a real advantage · Overall Ray Hotel's food has a clear strength at breakfast, while other meals are a convenient extra rather than the main reason people choose to stay

Service — Service is another point that earns consistent praise in real reviews · The front-desk staff are often described as friendly, warm, and helpful, especially with check-in, which many say is fast and hassle-free · The front desk is open 24 hours, so anyone arriving late after a match or a long trip doesn't need to worry · Some reviews also praise staff for giving good directions into the lane and tips on places to visit around Buriram · Check-in and check-out here are fairly flexible, generally check-in from the afternoon and check-out before noon or a little later · But to be straight about it, since it's a small hotel the on-site staff aren't as numerous as at a big hotel, so when many rooms check in at once — like on a big match day at Chang Arena — service can mean a bit of a wait at times · On the whole it's still a strength here and one reason the service score sits in good territory

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — Pulling from Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda, and Thai reviews on sites like Wongnai and Pantip, the picture lines up fairly well · On the praise side: a saltwater pool that doesn't sting and is easy to soak in, a gym with more machines than expected for the price, a varied breakfast with both Thai and Western food, clean and quiet rooms, friendly staff and fast check-in, free parking that's handy for self-drivers, and the overall value that has people calling it "hundred-baht prices, thousand-baht service" · On the note-to-self side: the most-mentioned issue is the narrow entrance lane that's hard to find the first time, with many saying they got lost following the map pin · Next is that some rooms are fairly dark with little natural light, the bedside lamps and outlets are limited, a few reviews found the air-con louder than expected, and the hotel's position — though in the city — isn't right by the dense restaurant areas, so you have to drive out for food in the evening · Most of these gripes are things you can solve by preparing before the trip and choosing your room, rather than major problems that keep people from coming back

"Clean room, quiet, comfortable to sleep in, breakfast had plenty to choose from and was filling, lovely staff who helped with directions into the lane · I'll come back next time but I'll note the route down first, because the first time I drove a little past the mouth of the lane."

Price and value compared — The starting price for a Deluxe Room is about THB 1,070–1,133/night in normal periods, and it can climb when there's a big event at Chang Arena, such as an important Thai League match day or a race weekend, when hotels across the city tend to fill up and prices rise together · Larger rooms like the Deluxe for 3 guests or the Family Room run from around THB 1,400 and up depending on size and timing · Compared with other 3-star hotels in Buriram city at the same price level, Ray Hotel feels very good value on amenities, especially getting a saltwater pool and a serious gym for just over a thousand baht, where many places at the same price offer only a small pool or no gym at all · If you weight getting into the pool, working out, and free parking above being next to restaurant areas or having a luxurious room, the money you spend here pays you back in full · But if your focus is stepping out of the hotel and finding food right away, or wanting the brightest and newest room, you may need to weigh it against other options in the city

What to know before booking — A few things make the stay smoother · One, prepare for the entrance — keep GPS running, drive slowly as you get close, and if you're unsure call the front desk, because the lane in is fairly narrow and hard to find the first time · Two, if you like a bright room or read before bed, try asking for a room that catches the sun and bring a power strip, since some rooms are fairly dark and bedside outlets are limited · Three, if you're coming for a match at Chang Arena, this location has the edge at only about 4 kilometres from the stadium, but book well ahead because on big match days hotels across the city fill up fast and prices rise · Four, if you plan to have dinner in the city, allow time to drive out, since the area around the hotel doesn't have dense restaurants · Five, check at booking whether the package includes breakfast, because breakfast here gets a lot of praise and is worth including · And pick free cancellation first if your plans aren't firm

The verdict — From all the real reviews, Ray Hotel Buriram is the best fit for anyone who wants to stay in Buriram city on a budget of just over a thousand baht but still get a saltwater pool, a serious gym, and free parking · The clear strengths are a set of amenities beyond the price, a pool that doesn't sting, a well-equipped gym, a varied breakfast, clean quiet rooms, and a location only about 4 kilometres from Chang Arena, which makes it worthwhile for families, fitness folks, and people coming for a match alike · If you're after luxury, a room that's bright and new in every corner, or stepping out the door into a sea of restaurants, this place may not be the answer, and you should consider a hotel in the heart of the commercial district instead · But for a Buriram trip where you want good value, a pool to soak in, a gym to work out in, and easy parking — Ray Hotel answers that need well at an accessible price, and it's why many guests call it "hundred-baht prices, thousand-baht service"
